## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A three-fascicle Tang-period translation by **Amoghavajra** ([不空](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%8D%E7%A9%BA)) of the *Mahā-vipula-mahā-maṇi-vimāna-supratiṣṭhita-guhya-dhāraṇī-sūtra* — the "Vast Great-Jewelled Pavilion" *dhāraṇī*-sūtra. The text presents an extensive *uṣṇīṣa* / *vipula-prāsāda* *dhāraṇī* together with an elaborate sūtra-frame narrative of cosmic-Buddha visions, jewelled-pavilion architectural visualisations, and the systematic generation of merit-empowered *dhāraṇī*-recitation practice.

**Abstract**

The *Vipula-prāsāda* sūtra constitutes one of the most expansive single-dhāraṇī scriptures in the Esoteric corpus. Its central *vipula-prāsāda dhāraṇī* — the "Vast-Pavilion" mantra — is associated with the visualisation of the cosmic *prāsāda* / *vimāna* (jewelled pavilion / palace) of all Buddhas, in which the practitioner mentally constructs a vast multi-levelled pavilion adorned with the seven jewels and inhabited by the Buddha-deities of all the cardinal and intermediate directions. The text is one of three principal Chinese recensions: Amoghavajra's T1005A (this text), Bodhiruci II's T1006 ([KR6j0199](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0199)), and the brief *fànběn* T1005B ([KR6j0198](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0198)). Composition falls in Amoghavajra's Cháng'ān period (746–774).
